Looking at them from the present, the Preceptor instructed pupils in the three virtues and the three…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
行之敎保氏有六藝六儀之敎大胥掌版小胥掌徵
樂德樂語樂舞之敎而又春秋詩書冬夏禮樂
令有觵撻之敎
崇其術也中年考校九年大成稽其業也
家塾黨庠術序國學廣其敎也其制可云
備矣及考戴記則天子視學大昕鼓徵衆
至然後天子至乃命有司行事興秩節祭
先聖先師焉必若並親之者何也天子建
維皇之極臣民所觀化者此也以故明王
===
===
重焉然又以關睢麟趾之意敷菁莪棫樸
之敎其化皆從心出玆所以天下順治而
享祚於靈長與自涿鹿之戰興而武功漸
啓往牒所紀帝王之武燦然矣試自明問
閱武者言之禹征苗而誓師湯伐夏而誓
衆蓋已肇訓武之端而周之法爲詳焉自
今觀之大司馬中春有振旅之典中夏有
茇舍之典中秋有治兵之典中冬則通三
時之敎有大閱之典而且坐作進退習其
punctuated:
行之敎，保氏有六藝六儀之敎，大胥掌版，小胥掌徵，樂德、樂語、樂舞之敎，而又春秋詩書，冬夏禮樂，令有觵撻之敎，崇其術也；中年考校，九年大成，稽其業也；家塾、黨庠、術序、國學，廣其敎也。其制可云備矣。及考《戴記》，則天子視學，大昕鼓徵，衆至，然後天子至，乃命有司行事，興秩節，祭先聖先師焉。必若並親之者，何也？天子建維皇之極，臣民所觀化者此也，以故明王重焉。然又以《關睢》《麟趾》之意，敷《菁莪》《棫樸》之敎，其化皆從心出，玆所以天下順治而享祚於靈長與？
自涿鹿之戰興，而武功漸啓，往牒所紀帝王之武燦然矣。試自明問閱武者言之，禹征苗而誓師，湯伐夏而誓衆，蓋已肇訓武之端，而周之法爲詳焉。自今觀之，大司馬中春有振旅之典，中夏有茇舍之典，中秋有治兵之典，中冬則通三時之敎，有大閱之典。而且坐作進退，習其
translation_en:
…instruction in the [three kinds of] conduct; the Junior Protector instructed pupils in the Six Arts and the six forms of deportment. The Senior Music Instructor kept the registers, and the Junior Music Instructor supervised the summoning of pupils. There was instruction in musical virtue, musical expression, and dance; moreover, poetry and documents were studied in spring and autumn, and rites and music in winter and summer. Regulations also provided correction through the penalty cup and the rod [?]: these measures elevated the methods of instruction. Examinations were held in the intervening years [?], and full accomplishment was attained after nine years: these measures assessed the pupils’ attainments. There were schools for households, schools in the dang neighborhoods, schools in the outlying districts [?], and schools in the capital: these extended instruction widely. Their system may indeed be called comprehensive.
When we consult the Record of Dai, we find that, when the Son of Heaven visited the school, a drum was sounded at early dawn to summon the assembly. Only after everyone had arrived did the Son of Heaven arrive. He then commanded the responsible officials to conduct the proceedings, setting the prescribed ceremonial observances in motion and sacrificing to the former sages and former teachers. Why was it necessary for him personally to attend to all these matters? The Son of Heaven established the sovereign’s supreme standard; it was to this that officials and people looked for moral transformation. For this reason, enlightened kings attached great importance to it. Moreover, they extended the teaching expressed in “Luxuriant Southernwood” and “The Oak Clumps” in the spirit of “The Ospreys” and “The Qilin’s Hoof.” Their transforming influence issued entirely from the heart. Was this not why all under Heaven was obedient and well governed, and why they enjoyed their blessed reigns for so long?
From the outbreak of the battle of Zhuolu, martial achievements gradually unfolded. Splendid indeed are the martial deeds of emperors and kings recorded in earlier histories. Let us address the review of military preparedness mentioned in your illuminating question. Yu swore an oath before his army when campaigning against the Miao, and Tang swore an oath before his host when attacking Xia. These already marked the beginnings of military training, but the methods of Zhou were more detailed. Viewed from the present, under the Grand Minister of War there was a prescribed exercise for marshaling the troops in mid-spring, one for encampment in mid-summer, and one for arraying the army in mid-autumn. In mid-winter, the training of the other three seasons was brought together in the grand review. Furthermore, in sitting and rising, advancing and retreating, they practiced their…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
節也鼓鐸鐲鐃審其聲也龍虎鳥龜辨其
象也其法信亦詳矣載考周禮振旅以苗
王執路鼓治兵以獮王載太常一歲四時
之教天子蓋再臨焉必若是親之者何也
天王爲紀法之宗華夷所瞻仰者此也以
故明王重焉然又天保以上治內采薇以
下治外其政皆由心立所以天下威嚴而
保泰於綿遠與裔兵而後漢高過魯祀聖
知崇道矣而自以馬上之治明帝臨雍拜
===
老知敦禮矣而□侈稽古之榮釋奠命講
孝經者唐太宗也而增廣生員罔裨仁義
之效幸學親贊孔顏者宋太祖也而州郡
立學未遑先事之圖其於古帝王純心之
學爲文教之本者槩乎未之聞也又烏能
與之儷美哉乃若立秋肄兵水南門此漢
制也而中平一講致貽蓋勳之譏立冬講
武都墠此唐制也而府兵三變竟滋杜牧
之嘆唐玄宗躬擐戎衣講武驪山而持鎗
punctuated:
節也，鼓鐸鐲鐃，審其聲也；龍虎鳥龜，辨其象也。其法信亦詳矣。載考《周禮》，振旅以苗，王執路鼓；治兵以獮，王載太常。一歲四時之教，天子蓋再臨焉。必若是親之者，何也？天王爲紀法之宗，華夷所瞻仰者此也，以故明王重焉。然又《天保》以上治內，《采薇》以下治外，其政皆由心立，所以天下威嚴而保泰於綿遠與！
裔兵而後，漢高過魯祀聖，知崇道矣，而自以馬上之治；明帝臨雍拜老，知敦禮矣，而□侈稽古之榮。釋奠命講《孝經》者，唐太宗也，而增廣生員，罔裨仁義之效；幸學親贊孔顏者，宋太祖也，而州郡立學，未遑先事之圖。其於古帝王純心之學爲文教之本者，槩乎未之聞也，又烏能與之儷美哉？
乃若立秋肄兵水南門，此漢制也，而中平一講，致貽蓋勳之譏；立冬講武都墠，此唐制也，而府兵三變，竟滋杜牧之嘆。唐玄宗躬擐戎衣，講武驪山，而持鎗
translation_en:
…their regulated movements; through drums, bells, and gongs, they distinguished the signals; through dragons, tigers, birds, and tortoises, they distinguished the emblems. These regulations were indeed detailed. Further examination of the Rites of Zhou shows that, when troops were marshaled for the summer hunt, the king held the great drum; when troops were drilled for the autumn hunt, the king bore the Great Constant banner. Thus, of the four seasonal training exercises each year, the Son of Heaven attended two in person. Why was such personal involvement necessary? The heavenly king was the fountainhead of rules and standards: it was to him that both the Chinese and the peoples beyond looked up. Enlightened kings therefore attached great importance to this. Moreover, the songs through “Heaven Protects” concerned ordering affairs within, while those from “Gathering Ferns” onward concerned ordering affairs without. Their government was established entirely from the heart. Was this not why their authority commanded awe throughout the realm and they preserved peace for ages?
After “yi bing” [?], Gaozu of Han passed through Lu and offered sacrifice to the Sage, showing that he knew to honor the Way; yet he himself relied on governing from horseback. Emperor Ming visited the Biyong academy and bowed to the elders, showing that he knew to uphold ritual; yet [illegible] he indulged in the glory of emulating antiquity. It was Taizong of Tang who ordered lectures on the Classic of Filial Piety at the offering ceremony to the sages; yet his expansion of student numbers did nothing to advance benevolence and righteousness. It was Taizu of Song who visited the school and personally composed praises of Confucius and Yan Hui; yet he found no time to plan ahead for establishing schools in the prefectures and commanderies. As for the ancient sage emperors’ learning that purified the heart and served as the foundation of civil instruction, these rulers seem never to have heard of it. How, then, could they equal the ancients in excellence?
As for drilling troops at the southern water gate at the Beginning of Autumn, this was a Han institution; yet a single review during the Zhongping reign incurred the criticism of Gai Xun. Holding military exercises at the capital’s drill ground at the Beginning of Winter was a Tang institution; yet three transformations of the militia system ultimately occasioned Du Mu’s lament. Xuanzong of Tang personally donned military dress and held exercises at Mount Li, yet, carrying a spear…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
立陣不幾於褻乎宋太宗堂名講武築於
西郊而劔舞鼓噪不比於戲乎其於古帝
王純心之學爲武功之本者藐乎未之得
也又奚能與之媲烈哉恭惟我
太祖高皇帝繼天立極
道冠皇王經緯天地之文未易殫述而崇儒
廣化尤軫
宸衷國子之學建於
登極之前三年州縣之學建於
===
開國之次年黌宮立
臥碑之訓
大誥著社學之章洋洋乎
皇極之敷也仰稽設兵之制則京營嚴操練之
律邊省備屯戍之規兵權統於夏卿戎籍
隸於五府兵政有統謨高千古其先天下
以開創者巍乎成底定之大業矣蓋我
高祖觀心有亭
存心有錄其所存者皆純天之心則夫軼三
punctuated:
立陣，不幾於褻乎？宋太宗堂名講武，築於西郊，而劔舞鼓噪，不比於戲乎？其於古帝王純心之學爲武功之本者，藐乎未之得也，又奚能與之媲烈哉？
恭惟我太祖高皇帝繼天立極，道冠皇王，經緯天地之文，未易殫述，而崇儒廣化，尤軫宸衷。國子之學建於登極之前三年，州縣之學建於開國之次年。黌宮立臥碑之訓，《大誥》著社學之章，洋洋乎皇極之敷也！仰稽設兵之制，則京營嚴操練之律，邊省備屯戍之規。兵權統於夏卿，戎籍隸於五府。兵政有統，謨高千古，其先天下以開創者，巍乎成底定之大業矣！蓋我高祖觀心有亭，存心有錄，其所存者皆純天之心，則夫軼三
translation_en:
…standing in battle formation—did this not verge on irreverence? Song Taizong built a hall in the western suburbs and named it “Military Training”; yet sword dancing, drumming, and shouting—were these not akin to playacting? He remained far from grasping the ancient sage-kings’ learning of purifying the mind as the foundation of military achievement. How, then, could he rival their accomplishments?
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, the Gao Emperor, succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard. His Way surpassed that of the august sovereigns and kings. His civil achievements in ordering Heaven and Earth cannot readily be recounted in full; yet honoring Confucian learning and extending moral transformation especially engaged his imperial concern. The Imperial University was established three years before his accession, and prefectural and county schools in the year following the founding of the dynasty. In the schools he erected the injunctions of the Recumbent Tablets, and in the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) he set forth provisions for community schools. How vast was this dissemination of the imperial standard!
Reverently examining his military institutions, we find that the capital garrisons had strict rules for drill, while the frontier provinces had comprehensive regulations for military colonies and garrison duty. Military authority was unified under the Minister of War, and military registers came under the Five Chief Military Commissions. Military administration thus had a unified structure, and his plans surpassed those of all preceding ages. In leading all under Heaven through the founding of the dynasty, he majestically accomplished the great undertaking of securing the realm!
Our Gaozu had a pavilion for contemplating the mind and a record for preserving the mind. What he preserved was wholly the mind of pure Heaven. Thus, in surpassing the Three …

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
五而獨隆者謂不有本與我
世宗肅皇帝應運嗣基
德超元始昭回雲漢之章未易罄陳而弘道
作人尤廑
聖慮
文華崇祀而
繼道統以綏猷
翊學有詩而揭心傳以範世
勅諭鐫於胄監
===
箴註布於膠庠煌煌乎懿德之肆也伏覩詰
戎之猷則咨邊計於大臣時蒙
宣召遴干城於武科屢
詔申嚴革監鎗坐營之蠹飭會官閱視之規經
武有要動出萬全其後天下以安成於契
乎光
紹述之丕圖矣蓋我
世宗敬一有箴
五箴有註其所存者即
punctuated: 五而獨隆者，謂不有本與？我世宗肅皇帝應運嗣基，德超元始，昭回雲漢之章，未易罄陳，而弘道作人尤廑聖慮。文華崇祀，而繼道統以綏猷；翊學有詩，而揭心傳以範世；勅諭鐫於胄監，箴註布於膠庠，煌煌乎懿德之肆也！伏覩詰戎之猷，則咨邊計於大臣，時蒙宣召；遴干城於武科，屢詔申嚴；革監鎗坐營之蠹，飭會官閱視之規。經武有要，動出萬全，其後天下以安成於契乎光紹述之丕圖矣。蓋我世宗敬一有箴，五箴有註，其所存者即
translation_en:
…the Five Emperors and stood alone in eminence: could one say that this had no foundation? Our Emperor Shizong, posthumously styled Su, answered the mandate of the age and succeeded to the throne. His virtue surpassed the primordial beginnings; his writings, shining like the Milky Way, cannot readily be recounted in full. Yet expanding the Way and cultivating worthy men were especially the objects of his sagely concern. He exalted sacrificial worship in the Wenhua Hall, continuing the succession of the Way to secure the principles of governance. He composed a poem on supporting learning, setting forth the transmission of the mind as a model for the world. His imperial admonitions were engraved at the Imperial University, and his commentaries on admonitions were distributed among the schools. How splendid was the unfolding of his admirable virtue!
Reverently observing his plans for military preparedness, we find that he consulted the high ministers on frontier strategy, repeatedly granting them imperial summons. To select men who would serve as shields and walls of the state through the military examinations, he repeatedly decreed that standards be rigorously enforced. He eliminated abuses associated with firearms supervision and resident camp commands, and tightened the regulations for joint inspections by officials. His management of military affairs grasped the essentials, and every action proceeded with complete provision for success. Coming later, he brought security to the realm and fulfilled the grand design of gloriously continuing his predecessors’ work [the wording here is garbled: ?]. For our Shizong composed an Admonition on Revering the One and supplied commentaries on the Five Admonitions. What he preserved in his heart was precisely…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
太祖之心則夫協先後於一揆者又不有自與
我
皇上誕膺寶曆
君師萬邦
憲章哲王匹休
先烈以文言之改元
恩詔昭垂
日月之光
御講
===
經筵妙契聖賢之蘊拔貢儒英而章縫荷澤
釐正文體而鉤棘還淳
文治則既熈矣竊聞紀元之年
駕幸太學
諭師生而
絲綸闡奧
謁先聖而俎豆增輝儒臣膺坐講之榮多士
蒙衣鈔之賚一時臣庶環橋門而觀聽者
宛然游成周之都聽奏公之美也禮臣因
punctuated:
太祖之心，則夫協先後於一揆者，又不有自與？

我皇上誕膺寶曆，君師萬邦，憲章哲王，匹休先烈。以文言之，改元恩詔，昭垂日月之光；御講經筵，妙契聖賢之蘊；拔貢儒英，而章縫荷澤；釐正文體，而鉤棘還淳。文治則既熈矣。竊聞紀元之年，駕幸太學，諭師生而絲綸闡奧，謁先聖而俎豆增輝。儒臣膺坐講之榮，多士蒙衣鈔之賚。一時臣庶環橋門而觀聽者，宛然游成周之都，聽奏公之美也。禮臣因
translation_en:
…the mind of Taizu. Does not this concord between predecessors and successors, measured by a single standard, therefore have its source?

Our Emperor has grandly assumed the imperial succession, serving as sovereign and teacher to the myriad realms, taking the wise kings as his models and matching the glory of his illustrious predecessors. To speak of civil accomplishments: his gracious edict inaugurating the reign shone with the radiance of the sun and moon; at the imperial lectures in the Classics Colloquium, he subtly grasped the profound meaning of the sages and worthies; he selected and advanced outstanding Confucian scholars, so that those wearing scholars’ caps received his bounty; and he rectified literary style, restoring simplicity where writing had become thorny and convoluted. Civil governance has thus already flourished.

Your servant has heard that, in the inaugural year of the reign, His Majesty visited the Imperial University. He instructed its teachers and students, his imperial words elucidating profound principles; he paid homage to the Former Sage, adding lustre to the sacrificial rites. Confucian officials received the honour of lecturing while seated, and the assembled scholars were bestowed clothing and paper currency. The officials and common people who gathered around the university’s Bridge Gate to watch and listen seemed to be wandering in the capital of Chengzhou, hearing the praises of the duke [?]. The officials responsible for rites thereupon…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
集之爲
聖駕臨雍錄昭示罔極化暢八埏不其紹
祖宗之聖文邪以武言之
軫懷九邊而頒
賜帑金更立三營而光復
祖制博選邊才以儲督撫慎遴邊吏以資保障
武烈則既揚矣復
俞輔臣之請
大閱六師
祭告行而百靈佑綏
鑾輿動而兩儀澄霽將士欽
諭戒之嚴中外服賞罰之允一時臣民見羽
旄而喜告者儼然際虞帝之廷覩舞干之
化也本兵因集之爲
大閱錄流播無窮
威覃九有不其纘
祖宗之神武邪愚又聞之天之陰陽非二也動
而爲陽而獨陽則不生靜而爲陰而獨陰
punctuated:
集之爲《聖駕臨雍錄》，昭示罔極，化暢八埏，不其紹祖宗之聖文邪？以武言之，軫懷九邊而頒賜帑金，更立三營而光復祖制，博選邊才以儲督撫，慎遴邊吏以資保障，武烈則既揚矣。復俞輔臣之請，大閱六師，祭告行而百靈佑綏，鑾輿動而兩儀澄霽，將士欽諭戒之嚴，中外服賞罰之允。一時臣民見羽旄而喜告者，儼然際虞帝之廷，覩舞干之化也。本兵因集之爲《大閱錄》，流播無窮，威覃九有，不其纘祖宗之神武邪？

愚又聞之，天之陰陽非二也。動而爲陽，而獨陽則不生；靜而爲陰，而獨陰
translation_en:
…compiled these events into the Record of the Imperial Visit to the Academy (Shengjia lin Yong lu), making the Emperor’s boundless beneficence manifest. His transforming influence reaches the eight extremities of the earth: does this not carry forward the sagely civil accomplishments of his imperial ancestors? As for military affairs, he has taken the Nine Frontier Garrisons to heart and bestowed funds from the imperial treasury; he has reestablished the Three Divisions, restoring the ancestral institutions. He has selected talented men widely from the frontiers to provide a reserve of supreme commanders and grand coordinators, and carefully chosen frontier officials to strengthen their defenses. His martial achievements have thus already been displayed. Further, he approved the request of his grand secretaries and held a grand review of the Six Armies. Sacrifices announcing the event were performed, and the hundred spirits bestowed protection and peace; the imperial carriage set forth, and Heaven and Earth became clear and bright. Officers and soldiers reverently received the stern imperial admonitions, while those at court and beyond acknowledged the fairness of rewards and punishments. The officials and common people who saw the feathered standards and joyfully spread the news seemed indeed to be present at the court of the Emperor of Yu, witnessing the transforming power of the dance with shields. The Minister of War accordingly compiled these events into the Record of the Grand Review (Da yue lu), to circulate for all time. His might extends throughout the nine regions: does this not continue the divine martial prowess of his imperial ancestors?

I have also heard that Heaven’s yin and yang are not two separate things. In movement it becomes yang, yet yang alone cannot engender life; in stillness it becomes yin, yet yin alone…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
則不成觀此而文武相須之義可識也天
之陰陽固一也陽主生育而聖人恒扶之
陰主肅殺而聖人恒抑之觀此而先德後
威之義可識也陰陽流行眞實無妄其天
之誠乎必文非彌文武非黷武而後爲憲
天之政焉陰陽動靜無非太極其天之心
乎必文思內蘊武毅中涵而後爲純天之
心焉史臣之贊堯也曰乃武乃文而放勳
不越乎欽詩人之咏文王也曰文武維后
===
而緝熈不外乎敬然則敬也者聖人希天
之學而
皇上所以纂
祖宗之盛兼帝王之隆者其本固在玆也愚生
跧伏草茅懷芹曝之忱久矣敢因執事爲
九重獻
第二問
吳永裕
同考試官教諭陳批近時文體多尚浮靡子能
punctuated:
則不成。觀此，而文武相須之義可識也。天之陰陽固一也，陽主生育，而聖人恒扶之；陰主肅殺，而聖人恒抑之。觀此，而先德後威之義可識也。陰陽流行，眞實無妄，其天之誠乎？必文非彌文，武非黷武，而後爲憲天之政焉。陰陽動靜，無非太極，其天之心乎？必文思內蘊，武毅中涵，而後爲純天之心焉。史臣之贊堯也，曰「乃武乃文」，而放勳不越乎欽；詩人之咏文王也，曰「文武維后」，而緝熈不外乎敬。然則敬也者，聖人希天之學，而皇上所以纂祖宗之盛、兼帝王之隆者，其本固在玆也。愚生跧伏草茅，懷芹曝之忱久矣，敢因執事爲九重獻。

第二問
吳永裕
同考試官教諭陳批：近時文體多尚浮靡，子能
translation_en:
…then nothing can reach completion. From this we may understand why civil and martial governance need one another. Heaven’s yin and yang are fundamentally one. Yang governs generation and nurture, and the sage constantly supports it; yin governs severity and destruction, and the sage constantly restrains it. From this we may understand why virtue should precede the exercise of awe-inspiring power. Yin and yang circulate, utterly real and without falsity: is this not Heaven’s sincerity? Only when civil governance avoids excessive ornament and martial governance avoids wanton warfare can government take Heaven as its model. The movement and stillness of yin and yang are all manifestations of the Supreme Ultimate: is this not Heaven’s heart? Only when cultivated thought is stored within and martial resolve is harbored inwardly can one’s heart be wholly in accord with Heaven.

In praising Yao, the court historian said, “Both martial and civil”; yet Yao’s illustrious achievements never went beyond reverence. In singing of King Wen, the poet said, “Civil and martial was our sovereign”; yet his continuing brightness never lay outside reverent attentiveness. Reverent attentiveness, then, is the learning through which the sage aspires to Heaven. Here indeed lies the foundation upon which His Majesty carries forward the splendor of his ancestors and unites the flourishing achievements of the ancient emperors and kings. I, an ignorant student living obscurely among the common people, have long cherished the sincere wish to offer my humble contribution—as one might offer celery or the warmth of the sun. Through you, honored officials, I venture to present it to the imperial throne.

Second Policy Question
Wu Yongyu
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Recent literary style has largely favored superficial ornament. You are able to…”

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
折衷歷代文章歸於簡實錄之
考試官學正何批文章之實用子能闡發其
切要而篇末轉移機括尤爲有見宜錄以式
考試官教諭艾批邇來士習浮靡奉
詔釐正誠復古之會也子欲敦本濟世其有志敬應者邪
文章之體貴敦本實而不以富麗炫工能
貴濟世務而不以浮靡事虛談此皆教化
之所係而治體之所趨也蓋文不根于本
實則雕蟲之技耳雖連篇累牘以侈其盛
===
而非所謂文也文罔裨于世務則虛車之
飾耳雖掇英擷華以萃其美而非所謂文
也故君子重有本之學治世無枝葉之言
而人才之盛衰世道之隆汙胥於文焉驗
之矣自今觀之尚書所載典謨訓誥唐虞
三代之文也讀其書于數千載之下猶可
以仰見其淳龐渾噩之氣象然說者謂六
經無文法三代無文人何也在上者以德
行用人未嘗以文舉士在下者以德行自
punctuated:
折衷歷代文章，歸於簡實，錄之。
考試官學正何批：文章之實用，子能闡發其切要，而篇末轉移機括，尤爲有見，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭艾批：邇來士習浮靡，奉詔釐正，誠復古之會也。子欲敦本濟世，其有志敬應者邪？
文章之體，貴敦本實，而不以富麗炫工能；貴濟世務，而不以浮靡事虛談。此皆教化之所係，而治體之所趨也。蓋文不根于本實，則雕蟲之技耳，雖連篇累牘以侈其盛，而非所謂文也；文罔裨于世務，則虛車之飾耳，雖掇英擷華以萃其美，而非所謂文也。故君子重有本之學，治世無枝葉之言，而人才之盛衰、世道之隆汙，胥於文焉驗之矣。自今觀之，《尚書》所載典謨訓誥，唐虞三代之文也。讀其書于數千載之下，猶可以仰見其淳龐渾噩之氣象。然說者謂六經無文法，三代無文人，何也？在上者以德行用人，未嘗以文舉士；在下者以德行自
translation_en:
…weigh the merits of the writings of successive dynasties and bring them back to simplicity and substance. Accept this essay.
Examiner He, an Instructor, comments: You can elucidate the essentials of writing’s practical utility. The pivotal turn at the end of the essay is especially perceptive. It should be included as a model.
Examiner Ai, an Instructor, comments: Recently, scholars’ habits have tended toward superficial extravagance. To correct them in obedience to the imperial edict is truly an opportunity to restore antiquity. You wish to strengthen the foundations and benefit the world: are you one resolved to respond reverently to this charge?
In its character, writing should prize strengthening foundations and substance, rather than displaying technical skill through richness and ornament; it should prize serving the affairs of the world, rather than indulging in empty discussion through superficial extravagance. These matters bear upon moral instruction and the direction of governance. For if writing is not rooted in foundations and substance, it is merely the trivial craft of carving insects. Though it fills successive essays and piles of documents to flaunt its abundance, it is not what deserves to be called writing. If writing contributes nothing to worldly affairs, it is merely ornament on an empty carriage [?]. Though it gathers blossoms and plucks flowers to concentrate their beauty, it is not what deserves to be called writing. Thus the gentleman values learning that has a foundation, and a well-governed age has no talk devoted merely to branches and leaves. The flourishing or decline of talent, and the elevation or debasement of the world’s moral condition, can all be assessed through writing.
Viewed from the present, the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations recorded in the Book of Documents are the writings of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Reading that book thousands of years later, one can still look up to its atmosphere of ample simplicity and uncontrived wholeness. Yet commentators say that the Six Classics have no rules of composition, and that the Three Dynasties had no literary specialists. Why is this? Those above employed people on the basis of virtue and conduct; they never selected scholars on the basis of literary composition. Those below, through virtue and conduct, themselves…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
立亦不知以文趨時故無意于求工也譬
之風行水上自然成文所以爲文之至也
周衰至于戰國學校之政不脩游士持縱
橫之議而上書求用策對之事已肇其端
漢以四科取士始爲對策射策遂成科舉
之習然經術時義固在也至隋始有進士
雖孝廉秀才未甞廢舉而相沿至唐詞賦
之科愈盛至宋則兼詞賦而又益以制誥
厥後罷明經而專重進士詞章之風日靡
===
靡焉無止極矣蓋上以此待天下之士而
天下之士亦以此應上之求昔人所謂今
之科舉不可如何之法也是亦因時之制
也然漢廷親策賢良方正皆因事而舉若
置朔方問鹽鐵均輸榷酤罷行之宜皆當
時大事令建議之臣與之反覆詰難卒用
其言罷榷酤而天下稱便此豈取其文辭
已哉蓋漢儒去古未遠所學即所言所言
即所用非若後之徒事于文者也唐藝文
punctuated:
立，亦不知以文趨時，故無意于求工也。譬之風行水上，自然成文，所以爲文之至也。周衰，至于戰國，學校之政不脩，游士持縱橫之議而上書求用，策對之事已肇其端。漢以四科取士，始爲對策、射策，遂成科舉之習，然經術時義固在也。至隋始有進士，雖孝廉、秀才未甞廢舉，而相沿至唐，詞賦之科愈盛。至宋，則兼詞賦而又益以制誥。厥後罷明經而專重進士，詞章之風日靡靡焉，無止極矣。蓋上以此待天下之士，而天下之士亦以此應上之求。昔人所謂今之科舉不可如何之法也，是亦因時之制也。
然漢廷親策賢良方正，皆因事而舉，若置朔方，問鹽鐵、均輸、榷酤罷行之宜，皆當時大事。令建議之臣與之反覆詰難，卒用其言罷榷酤，而天下稱便，此豈取其文辭已哉？蓋漢儒去古未遠，所學即所言，所言即所用，非若後之徒事于文者也。唐藝文
translation_en:
…established themselves, nor did they think to use literary composition to accommodate the fashions of the time; thus they had no deliberate intention of seeking stylistic polish. It was like wind moving over water, naturally forming patterns: this is what made their writing the highest achievement.
As the Zhou declined and the Warring States period arrived, the administration of schools fell into neglect. Itinerant persuaders advanced proposals for vertical and horizontal alliances and submitted writings seeking employment. Here the practice of answering policy questions had already begun. The Han selected men through four categories and introduced both responses to policy questions and questions drawn by lot, thereby establishing the practice of examination recruitment. Yet classical learning and the concerns of the times still had their place. Only under the Sui did the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) category first appear. Although recommendations of the Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian) and the Flourishing Talent (xiucai) were never abandoned, as these practices continued into the Tang, the examination category for poetry and rhapsodies grew ever more prominent. Under the Song, poetry and rhapsodies were retained, and the drafting of imperial decrees and proclamations was added. Subsequently, the Illuminating the Classics (mingjing) category was abolished and exclusive emphasis placed on the jinshi category. The fashion for ornate composition became daily more decadent, without limit.
Those above treated the scholars of the realm in this way, and the scholars of the realm responded accordingly to the demands of those above. This is what an earlier writer meant by calling the examinations of his day a system about which nothing could be done. This, too, was an institution adapted to its times.
Yet when the Han court personally examined those recommended as Worthy and Good, Upright and Rectilinear (xianliang fangzheng), it always did so in response to particular affairs. Such matters as establishing Shuofang and asking whether the salt and iron monopolies, equitable transport system, and liquor monopoly should be abolished or maintained were all major issues of the day. The court had the ministers who proposed these policies repeatedly question and debate the respondents. In the end, it adopted their advice and abolished the liquor monopoly, a measure acclaimed throughout the realm as beneficial. Could this have been merely a matter of valuing their literary expression? The Han Confucian scholars were not far removed from antiquity: what they studied was what they said, and what they said was what they put into practice. They were unlike those of later times who devoted themselves solely to literary composition. The Tang account of literary writing …

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
傳論唐之文無慮三變王楊爲之伯燕許
擅其宗韓柳造其極然務求巧麗以此爲
賢溺于所習悉昧本源趙臣病其有五弊
而唐之文可知已趙子直論宋之文淳厚
見于立國之初中正作于慶曆之際矯激
起于熈寧之後然必如歐陽脩知貢舉而
後變鉤棘爲渾厚革險恠爲醇雅則宋之
文可知已至于文辭奇敘意通宜深宜易
當對不當對非文之六說乎如成周如七
===
國如西漢非文之三等乎宜雅宜理尚實
尚麗非文之四科乎易見易識易讀非文
之三易乎是皆論爲文之體裁品格而移
風救弊之道亦在其中矣我
國家設科取士首崇經術以明經爲第一義
觀其心得義理之學繼用策論詢以古訓
時務而究其博通古今明體適用之效二
百餘年豪俊之士垂功名于竹帛勒勛業
于鼎彝雲蒸霧集率登是選卽古師師濟
punctuated:
傳論唐之文，無慮三變：王楊爲之伯，燕許擅其宗，韓柳造其極。然務求巧麗，以此爲賢，溺于所習，悉昧本源。趙臣病其有五弊，而唐之文可知已。趙子直論宋之文，淳厚見于立國之初，中正作于慶曆之際，矯激起于熈寧之後。然必如歐陽脩知貢舉，而後變鉤棘爲渾厚，革險恠爲醇雅，則宋之文可知已。至于文辭奇、敘意通、宜深、宜易、當對、不當對，非文之六說乎？如成周，如七國，如西漢，非文之三等乎？宜雅、宜理、尚實、尚麗，非文之四科乎？易見、易識、易讀，非文之三易乎？是皆論爲文之體裁品格，而移風救弊之道亦在其中矣。
我國家設科取士，首崇經術，以明經爲第一義，觀其心得義理之學；繼用策論，詢以古訓時務，而究其博通古今、明體適用之效。二百餘年，豪俊之士垂功名于竹帛，勒勛業于鼎彝，雲蒸霧集，率登是選。卽古師師濟
translation_en:
…the discussion in the biographies states that Tang writing underwent, broadly speaking, three transformations: Wang and Yang became its leaders; Yan and Xu commanded its principal tradition; and Han and Liu brought it to its pinnacle. Yet writers strove for ingenuity and elegance, regarding these as excellence; absorbed in their accustomed practices, they entirely lost sight of the source. Zhao Chen [?] deplored its five defects. From this, the character of Tang writing can be understood. Zhao Zizhi, discussing Song writing, held that simplicity and substance appeared at the dynasty’s founding, balance and correctness arose during the Qingli era, and strained excess emerged after the Xining era. Yet only when someone such as Ouyang Xiu supervised the examinations could tangled, thorny writing be transformed into fullness and substance, and outlandish obscurity into purity and refinement. From this, the character of Song writing can be understood. As for unusual diction, clear expression of meaning, appropriate profundity, appropriate simplicity, occasions for parallel phrasing, and occasions for avoiding it—are these not the six propositions concerning writing? Writing modeled on the mature Zhou, the Seven States, and the Western Han—are these not its three grades? Requiring refinement, requiring coherence, valuing substance, and valuing elegance—are these not its four categories? Being easy to apprehend, easy to understand, and easy to read—are these not its three kinds of ease? These all concern the forms and qualities of composition, yet within them also lies the way to transform prevailing habits and remedy abuses.
Our dynasty established examinations to select men for service, giving foremost honor to classical learning. It makes understanding the Classics its first principle, examining candidates’ personal grasp of moral principles. It then employs policy essays and discourses, questioning them about ancient teachings and contemporary affairs, to investigate how effectively they comprehend past and present, understand fundamental principles, and apply them appropriately. For more than two hundred years, outstanding men have left their achievements and reputations in the historical record and had their meritorious deeds inscribed on ritual vessels. Gathering like rising clouds and assembling mist, they have generally advanced through this selection. Even the ancients’ multitude of mutually emulating worthies…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
濟籲俊菁莪之盛亦何以過之顧邇年以
來漸異昔時士爲文自質實而華麗自華
麗而浮泛自簡勁而暢達自暢達而繁冗
不繹聖賢之旨而崇記誦之時義習爲故
常剽竊成風甘心籬下之寄而不耻不察
時勢之宜而泥口耳之舊聞採其近似鋪
敘成篇咸老生之常談而自爲博雅經義
靡所發明治體殊無考見士習吏治亦因
之日就草略而
===
國家設科之美意竟爲虛文此亦趙臣之所
患而歐陽之所欲釐正者也近言官睍見
時弊
奏行文體限字之式我
皇上業已
俞允行令嚴飭彰示學校之士而輔臣又
奏令人臣建白章疏悉歸簡明我
皇上復
賜
punctuated:
濟，籲俊、菁莪之盛，亦何以過之？顧邇年以來，漸異昔時。士爲文，自質實而華麗，自華麗而浮泛；自簡勁而暢達，自暢達而繁冗。不繹聖賢之旨，而崇記誦之時義，習爲故常，剽竊成風，甘心籬下之寄而不耻；不察時勢之宜，而泥口耳之舊聞，採其近似，鋪敘成篇，咸老生之常談，而自爲博雅。經義靡所發明，治體殊無考見，士習吏治亦因之日就草略，而國家設科之美意竟爲虛文。此亦趙臣之所患，而歐陽之所欲釐正者也。
近言官睍見時弊，奏行文體限字之式。我皇上業已俞允，行令嚴飭，彰示學校之士。而輔臣又奏令人臣建白章疏悉歸簡明，我皇上復賜
translation_en:
…with their abundant ranks of worthy men, their summoning of outstanding talent, and their flourishing cultivation of scholars celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood”—how could even those ancient achievements surpass this? Yet in recent years things have gradually departed from former practice. In their writing, scholars have moved from substance and solidity to ornate elegance, and from ornate elegance to superficiality; from concision and vigor to fluency, and from fluency to prolixity. Instead of elucidating the purport of the sages and worthies, they prize memorized examination essays on the Classics. Repetition has become established practice, and plagiarism the prevailing fashion. They willingly lodge beneath another’s fence, without shame. Instead of examining what present circumstances require, they cling to stale information passed from mouth to ear, select whatever seems approximately relevant, and elaborate it into an essay. It is all the commonplace talk of old pedants, yet they consider themselves learned and refined. They shed no light on the meaning of the Classics and display no investigated understanding of the essentials of government. Consequently, scholarly practices and official administration grow more careless by the day, while the state’s fine intention in establishing the examinations ultimately becomes an empty formality. This, too, is what the minister Zhao worried about and what Ouyang wished to rectify.
Recently, officials charged with remonstrance, perceiving [?] the abuses of the day, memorialized requesting the implementation of rules governing prose style and limiting the number of characters. Our Emperor has already approved this and issued orders for strict enforcement, making the rules clearly known to students in the schools. The grand secretaries further memorialized requesting that all memorials in which officials submit proposals be concise and clear. Our Emperor again bestowed…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
俞允卽行
禁諭昭布中外臣工蓋欲盡返故習一歸簡
實其
明時復古之會乎愚則以爲性理之文宜精研
議論之文尚簡切大羹玄酒以爲味一唱
三歎以爲音溫潤和粹以爲氣淡泊平中
以爲辭剴切直陳以爲義而悠然渾然者
不可變也厲之以穀梁暢之以孟荀肆之
以老莊博之以國語致之以離騷著之以
===
太史公而淵然蒼然者不可易也如朱子
所謂治世之文可也如程子所謂名世傳
世之文可也寧爲菽粟布帛而不爲玉珮
瓊琚寧爲灝灝噩噩而不爲長江大河如
是而敷陳經義闡明理道之精微論議治
體有裨時勢之切要所言皆可實用而文
非操觚之藝矣此愚之所願學者也雖然
又有說焉漢武好浮誇而相如以浮誇應
魏帝好浮靡而曹植以浮靡應此興彼效
punctuated:
俞允，卽行禁諭，昭布中外臣工，蓋欲盡返故習，一歸簡實。其明時復古之會乎？

愚則以爲，性理之文宜精研，議論之文尚簡切。大羹玄酒以爲味，一唱三歎以爲音，溫潤和粹以爲氣，淡泊平中以爲辭，剴切直陳以爲義，而悠然渾然者不可變也。厲之以穀梁，暢之以孟荀，肆之以老莊，博之以國語，致之以離騷，著之以太史公，而淵然蒼然者不可易也。如朱子所謂治世之文可也，如程子所謂名世傳世之文可也。寧爲菽粟布帛，而不爲玉珮瓊琚；寧爲灝灝噩噩，而不爲長江大河。如是而敷陳經義，闡明理道之精微，論議治體，有裨時勢之切要，所言皆可實用，而文非操觚之藝矣。此愚之所願學者也。

雖然，又有說焉。漢武好浮誇，而相如以浮誇應；魏帝好浮靡，而曹植以浮靡應。此興彼效，
translation_en:
…granted approval, and the prohibitory injunctions were immediately put into effect and publicly proclaimed to officials at court and in the provinces. The intention was surely to reverse established habits entirely and bring everything back to simplicity and substance. Is this not an occasion for restoring antiquity in an enlightened age?

In my humble view, writings on human nature and principle require meticulous investigation, while argumentative writings should prize concision and pertinence. Let their flavor be that of unseasoned broth and plain water offered in sacrifice; their sound, that of one singer answered by three voices; their vital spirit, warm, gentle, harmonious, and pure; their diction, unadorned, even, and balanced; and their meaning, pertinent and directly expressed. Yet their unhurried ease and integral wholeness must remain unchanged. Sharpen them through the Guliang Commentary, give them fluency through Mencius and Xunzi, freedom through Laozi and Zhuangzi, breadth through the Discourses of the States, refinement through Encountering Sorrow (Li sao), and clarity through the Grand Astrologer, Sima Qian. Yet their depth and antique dignity must remain unaltered. Writing such as Master Zhu called “the writing of an age of good government” would suffice; writing such as Master Cheng called “writing that wins renown in its age and is transmitted to later ages” would suffice. Better beans and grain, cloth and silk, than jade pendants and precious ornaments; better vast simplicity and solemn grandeur than the rushing sweep of the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers. In this way, one may expound the meaning of the classics, illuminate the subtleties of principle and the Way, and discuss the essentials of government so as to contribute to the pressing needs of the times. Everything said would have practical application, and writing would then be more than the craft of wielding a writing tablet. This is what I humbly wish to learn.

Nevertheless, there is a further point to make. Emperor Wu of Han favored extravagant boasting, and Sima Xiangru responded with extravagant boasting; the emperor of Wei favored frivolous ornament, and Cao Zhi responded with frivolous ornament. What the one encouraged, the other imitated…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
捷如影響可見轉移變易之機括在上不
在下矣仰惟
朝廷重體要之辭崇責實之政鼓舞之機真
足以示
代之章程而激天下之敬應由是喜議論
者息其浮言競詞藻者還于淳朴挽士習
而復隆古人文之化端在斯矣愚何幸躬
逢其盛
第三問
===
陳嘉賓
同考試官教諭楊 批 敷答明悉趨向端正是能
志伊甫之志者
同考試官教諭王 批 尚論古賢哲而歸本才德
合一真知要之言也錄之
同考試官學正張 批 發先哲之蘊晰王霸之幾
子其深有志於尚友者乎
考試官學正何 批 條答允當
考試官教諭艾 批 品藻詳明
punctuated:
捷如影響，可見轉移變易之機括在上不在下矣。仰惟朝廷重體要之辭，崇責實之政，鼓舞之機，真足以示代之章程，而激天下之敬應。由是喜議論者息其浮言，競詞藻者還于淳朴，挽士習而復隆古人文之化，端在斯矣。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第三問

陳嘉賓

同考試官教諭楊批：「敷答明悉，趨向端正，是能志伊甫之志者。」

同考試官教諭王批：「尚論古賢哲，而歸本才德合一，真知要之言也。錄之。」

同考試官學正張批：「發先哲之蘊，晰王霸之幾，子其深有志於尚友者乎！」

考試官學正何批：「條答允當。」

考試官教諭艾批：「品藻詳明。」
translation_en:
…as swiftly as a shadow follows its form or an echo its sound. This shows that the mechanism for redirecting and transforming customs lies with those above, not those below. I reverently consider how the court values language that embodies essentials and honors government that demands substantive results. Its power to inspire is truly sufficient to set standards for the age [?] and elicit a reverent response throughout the realm. Consequently, those fond of argument will cease their empty talk, and those competing in verbal ornament will return to simplicity. The means to reform scholars’ habits and restore the civilizing influence of high antiquity lie precisely here. How fortunate I am personally to witness such flourishing!

Third Question

Chen Jiabin

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “His exposition and answers are clear and thorough, and his aspirations upright. Here is someone capable of taking the aspirations of Yi and Fu as his own.”

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “He discusses the worthies and sages of antiquity, grounding his argument in the unity of ability and virtue. These are truly the words of someone who understands what is essential. Accept this essay.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: “He reveals the profound insights of earlier sages and clarifies the subtle distinction between kingly and hegemonic rule. Surely you aspire deeply to taking the ancients as your friends!”

Examiner He, School Director, comments: “His answers to the individual points are sound and appropriate.”

Examiner Ai, Instructor, comments: “His evaluations are detailed and clear.”

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
甞謂古之大臣懋建勳猷光昭聲實而惠
澤流於當時風烈垂于後世者豈有他哉
要惟本之以德而濟之以才焉耳何謂德
契理道之蘊而戴仁抱義以成天下之大
忠者是也何謂才攄經濟之略而宣力効
能以弘天下之大業者是也故有德以達
才則見諸寅亮者不爲無本有才以宣德
則畜諸淵懿者不爲無具此古之名卿鉅
輔所以弼成有道之治而至今仰休光者
===
不衰也執事策士而以中土相業下詢承
學毋亦以諸生中有夙抱先憂式追往哲
者乎而愚非其人也敢不掇拾以對甞聞
有一代帝王之興必有一代帝王之佐雲
龍風虎勢相景從蓋自古已然矣惟玆河
南古豫州也居天地四方之中帶嵩邙河
洛之勝孕靈毓秀賢哲挺生以故理學闡
其淵源經制擅其勳烈文章燁其精華剛
大抒其節氣其間元臣碩輔柄鈞衡而翼
punctuated:
甞謂古之大臣，懋建勳猷，光昭聲實，而惠澤流於當時，風烈垂于後世者，豈有他哉？要惟本之以德，而濟之以才焉耳。何謂德？契理道之蘊，而戴仁抱義，以成天下之大忠者是也。何謂才？攄經濟之略，而宣力効能，以弘天下之大業者是也。故有德以達才，則見諸寅亮者不爲無本；有才以宣德，則畜諸淵懿者不爲無具。此古之名卿鉅輔所以弼成有道之治，而至今仰休光者不衰也。
執事策士，而以中土相業下詢承學，毋亦以諸生中有夙抱先憂、式追往哲者乎？而愚非其人也，敢不掇拾以對？甞聞有一代帝王之興，必有一代帝王之佐。雲龍風虎，勢相景從，蓋自古已然矣。惟玆河南，古豫州也，居天地四方之中，帶嵩邙河洛之勝，孕靈毓秀，賢哲挺生。以故理學闡其淵源，經制擅其勳烈，文章燁其精華，剛大抒其節氣。其間元臣碩輔，柄鈞衡而翼
translation_en:
I have often said: when the great ministers of antiquity diligently established meritorious achievements and wise policies, made both their reputations and their actual accomplishments shine forth, bestowed benefits upon their contemporaries, and left an exemplary legacy to later generations, was there any other explanation? The essential point was simply that they took virtue as their foundation and complemented it with ability. What is virtue? It is comprehending the profound meaning of principle and the Way, upholding benevolence and embracing righteousness, and thereby achieving the utmost loyalty in service to all under Heaven. What is ability? It is deploying strategies for ordering the realm, exerting oneself and putting one’s capabilities to use, and thereby advancing the great enterprise of all under Heaven. Thus, when virtue enables ability to find expression, the reverent assistance offered to the ruler has a foundation; when ability gives effect to virtue, the profound excellence cultivated within has the means to act. This is why the renowned ministers and great counsellors of antiquity helped bring about government in accordance with the Way, and why admiration for their glorious example has endured to this day.
You, sir, in examining scholars through policy questions, have graciously asked us students about the achievements of chief ministers from the Central Lands. Might this be because you believe that among us are those who have long cherished the resolve to take on the realm’s anxieties before others and to follow the wise men of the past? Though I am not such a person, how could I fail to gather what I can in reply? I have heard that whenever imperial rulers arise in an age, there must also be ministers of that age to assist them. As clouds follow dragons and winds follow tigers, they naturally follow one another like shadows. This has been so since antiquity. Now Henan was anciently Yuzhou. Situated at the center of Heaven and Earth and the four quarters, it embraces the scenic grandeur of Mount Song, Mount Mang, the Yellow River, and the Luo River. Nurturing spiritual potency and outstanding gifts, it has brought forth eminent worthies and sages. Thus, in the learning of principle they elucidated its profound sources; in institutions of government they distinguished themselves through meritorious achievements; in literary composition they displayed brilliant refinement; and through firmness and greatness of spirit they expressed their integrity and moral vigor. Among them were eminent ministers and great counsellors who wielded the authority of chief ministers and assisted …

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
贊鴻業者誠聲光相望更僕未易數矣姑
卽明問相業彪炳者陳之吾於商得伊尹
焉耕莘守一介之節應聘任天下之重伊
訓一書爲法萬世非天民之先覺乎於周
得山甫焉進能保王德之媺退能補袞職
之闕烝民一詩允輔中興非周邦之良翰
乎聽政三年而百姓頌其德子產所以見
稱于孔子也位居令尹而楚王因以伯叔
敖所以見重於虞丘也春秋之功業其容
===
掩乎交懽周勃卒能安劉陳平六出奇計
之餘也同心宋璟輔治開元姚崇十事要
說之效也漢唐之謀略孰能先乎遇事敢
言三居相位者吕蒙正也儉約好學至老
不倦者宋庠也二人皆以狀元位宰相不
愧科名克樹大節論者信不能優劣矣唱
名雲見位兼將相者韓琦也使虜抗詞功
存社稷者富弼也二人皆以元老建奇功
國之蓍蔡民之父母論者亦不容軒輊矣
punctuated: 贊鴻業者，誠聲光相望，更僕未易數矣。姑卽明問相業彪炳者陳之：吾於商得伊尹焉，耕莘守一介之節，應聘任天下之重，《伊訓》一書，爲法萬世，非天民之先覺乎？於周得山甫焉，進能保王德之媺，退能補袞職之闕，《烝民》一詩，允輔中興，非周邦之良翰乎？聽政三年，而百姓頌其德，子產所以見稱于孔子也；位居令尹，而楚王因以伯，叔敖所以見重於虞丘也。春秋之功業，其容掩乎？交懽周勃，卒能安劉，陳平六出奇計之餘也；同心宋璟，輔治開元，姚崇十事要說之效也。漢唐之謀略，孰能先乎？遇事敢言，三居相位者，吕蒙正也；儉約好學，至老不倦者，宋庠也。二人皆以狀元位宰相，不愧科名，克樹大節，論者信不能優劣矣。唱名雲見，位兼將相者，韓琦也；使虜抗詞，功存社稷者，富弼也。二人皆以元老建奇功，國之蓍蔡，民之父母，論者亦不容軒輊矣。
translation_en:
…assisted the great imperial enterprise. Indeed, their renown and glory followed one another in succession; even with relays of attendants, they could hardly be enumerated. Let me therefore address your illuminating question by setting forth those whose achievements as chief ministers were outstanding.

In the Shang, I find Yi Yin. While farming at Shen, he maintained scrupulous integrity; when summoned to service, he shouldered responsibility for all under Heaven. His Instructions of Yi (Yi xun) became a model for ten thousand generations. Was he not the first to awaken among Heaven’s people? In the Zhou, I find Shanfu. At court he preserved the excellence of the king’s virtue; away from court he remedied deficiencies in the royal office. The poem Multitudes of the People (Zheng min) attests that he truly assisted the restoration of the dynasty. Was he not a worthy pillar of the Zhou state?

After he had administered government for three years, the people praised his virtue: this was why Zichan won Confucius’s commendation. He held the office of Chief Minister, and through him the king of Chu attained hegemony: this was why Shu’ao was esteemed by Yuqiu. Could the achievements of these men of the Spring and Autumn period possibly be obscured?

By cultivating friendship with Zhou Bo, he ultimately secured the Liu ruling house: this was a further achievement of Chen Ping beyond his six extraordinary stratagems. By working in harmony with Song Jing, he assisted the good government of the Kaiyuan era: this was the effect of Yao Chong’s ten essential proposals. Who could surpass these men of the Han and Tang in strategic wisdom?

The man who dared to speak out when matters arose and served three times as chief minister was Lü Mengzheng. The man who lived frugally, loved learning, and remained tireless into old age was Song Xiang. Both rose from first place in the Palace Examination to become chief ministers. They lived up to their examination distinction and established exemplary integrity. Those who judge them truly cannot rank one above the other.

The man at whose proclamation of examination rank a cloud appeared [?], and who held both military and chief ministerial office, was Han Qi. The man who spoke firmly while serving as envoy to the northern foes and whose achievements preserved the state was Fu Bi. Both, as elder statesmen, accomplished extraordinary deeds. They were the state’s divining stalks and tortoise shells—its trusted guides—and the people’s fathers and mothers. Those who judge them likewise cannot place one above the other.

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
凡此數君子者或崛起於千百載之上而
隆古仰其烈或興起于千百載之後而當
世揚其休雖事功不能盡同而要皆才德
爲之用也逮及我
朝稽古定制革前代丞相中書之府
召選卿佐入輔大政卽宰相職也
列聖以來人文丕英一時輔弼諸臣應運而生
者其在
憲宗時則有若李賢其人焉初典銓司荐陟政
===
===
府雖閎業之著於
兩朝者不暇悉舉卽如政本十事稱爲至論
安邊十策多見施行非所謂嘉謀嘉猷入
告爾后音乎其謚文達宜矣在
孝宗時則有若劉健其人焉蚤儲翰苑尋簡
內閣雖偉績之昭於
兩朝者不暇悉陳卽如憫四方之荐災而屢
疏時宜當貂璫之內訌而抗章力諫非所
謂邦國儀刑老成馮翼者乎謚以文靖當
punctuated:
凡此數君子者，或崛起於千百載之上，而隆古仰其烈；或興起于千百載之後，而當世揚其休。雖事功不能盡同，而要皆才德爲之用也。逮及我朝，稽古定制，革前代丞相中書之府，召選卿佐入輔大政，卽宰相職也。列聖以來，人文丕英，一時輔弼諸臣應運而生者，其在憲宗時，則有若李賢其人焉。初典銓司，荐陟政府。雖閎業之著於兩朝者，不暇悉舉，卽如政本十事，稱爲至論；安邊十策，多見施行。非所謂「嘉謀嘉猷，入告爾后音」乎？其謚文達宜矣。
在孝宗時，則有若劉健其人焉。蚤儲翰苑，尋簡內閣。雖偉績之昭於兩朝者，不暇悉陳，卽如憫四方之荐災，而屢疏時宜；當貂璫之內訌，而抗章力諫。非所謂「邦國儀刑，老成馮翼」者乎？謚以文靖，當
translation_en:
Of these several gentlemen, some rose to prominence hundreds or thousands of years ago, and in distant antiquity their achievements were admired [?]; others arose hundreds or thousands of years later, and their contemporaries celebrated their excellence. Although their accomplishments could not all be the same, in essence all put their talent and virtue to use. When our dynasty came, it consulted antiquity to establish its institutions, abolishing the offices of Chief Councilor and the Central Secretariat inherited from preceding dynasties. It selected and summoned ministers to assist in the great affairs of government: this was precisely the function of a chief councilor. Under successive sage emperors, men of outstanding cultivation flourished; among the ministers who arose in response to the needs of their age to assist the throne, there was, during Xianzong’s reign, a man such as Li Xian. He first presided over personnel selection and subsequently rose to the highest councils of government. There is no time to enumerate all the great achievements that distinguished his service under two emperors. Take simply his ten proposals on the foundations of government, acclaimed as consummate judgments, and his ten policies for securing the frontiers, many of which were implemented. Was this not what is meant by ‘Present your excellent plans and counsels to your ruler’ [?]? His posthumous title, Wenda—‘Cultured and Accomplished’—was fitting indeed.
During Xiaozong’s reign, there was a man such as Liu Jian. Early on he was nurtured in the Hanlin Academy, and before long he was selected for the Grand Secretariat. There is no time to recount fully the magnificent accomplishments that shone forth under two emperors. Take simply how, distressed by repeated disasters throughout the realm, he repeatedly submitted memorials on measures appropriate to the times; and how, amid internal strife among the eunuchs, he boldly submitted memorials and remonstrated forcefully. Was he not what is meant by ‘a model for the realm, a seasoned elder to rely upon for support’? To confer upon him the posthumous title Wenjing—‘Cultured and Tranquil’—was fitting …

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣夫即此二君子者以考諸前代其亦聞
伊甫之風而興起者乎而韓富諸臣誠不
得專其美矣迺執事猶欲責諸生以尚友
之學顧生也不敏孰從而學之蓋兼多才
者所以會其全而集衆善者爲能成其大
乃若文達文靖二臣耳目未遠儀刑具在
無容贅矣至于韓琦吾取其定策之勳焉
富弼吾取其使虜之節焉蒙正吾取其量
宋庠吾取其直焉陳平姚崇吾取其應變
===
之略焉叔敖之執法吾取其貞焉子產之
愛人吾取其惠焉等而上之仲山甫之柔
亦不茹剛亦不吐伊尹之先知覺後知先
覺覺後覺是則王者之佐三代之英也能
無景行之思乎詩曰德輶如毛仲山甫舉
之書曰惟尹躬暨湯咸有一德則德也者
二臣勳業之本也推之而伐夏救民相湯
以王天下推之而保王躬式百辟賦明命
于四方莫非德之用也而王佐之才不能
punctuated: 矣。夫即此二君子者，以考諸前代，其亦聞伊甫之風而興起者乎？而韓富諸臣誠不得專其美矣。迺執事猶欲責諸生以尚友之學，顧生也不敏，孰從而學之？蓋兼多才者，所以會其全；而集衆善者，爲能成其大。乃若文達、文靖二臣，耳目未遠，儀刑具在，無容贅矣。至于韓琦，吾取其定策之勳焉；富弼，吾取其使虜之節焉；蒙正，吾取其量；宋庠，吾取其直焉；陳平、姚崇，吾取其應變之略焉；叔敖之執法，吾取其貞焉；子產之愛人，吾取其惠焉。等而上之，仲山甫之柔亦不茹、剛亦不吐，伊尹之先知覺後知、先覺覺後覺，是則王者之佐、三代之英也，能無景行之思乎？《詩》曰：「德輶如毛，仲山甫舉之。」《書》曰：「惟尹躬暨湯，咸有一德。」則德也者，二臣勳業之本也。推之而伐夏救民，相湯以王天下；推之而保王躬，式百辟，賦明命于四方，莫非德之用也，而王佐之才不能
translation_en:
…was fitting. If we compare these two gentlemen with men of earlier ages, were they not also inspired to action upon hearing of the exemplary conduct of Yi Yin and Zhongshan Fu? Han Qi, Fu Bi, and the other ministers certainly cannot claim exclusive possession of such excellence. Yet you, honored examiners, still wish to require us students to pursue the learning of taking the ancients as friends. But I am slow of understanding: whom should I follow and learn from? For it is by combining many talents that one attains completeness, and by gathering together many virtues that one achieves greatness. As for the two ministers posthumously titled Wenda and Wenjing, they are still within recent memory, and their exemplary conduct remains fully before us; there is no need to elaborate.
As for Han Qi, I would emulate his meritorious service in settling the imperial succession; from Fu Bi, his steadfast integrity as an envoy to the barbarians; from Mengzheng, his magnanimity; from Song Xiang, his uprightness; and from Chen Ping and Yao Chong, their resourcefulness in responding to changing circumstances. In Shu’ao’s enforcement of the law, I would emulate his rectitude; in Zichan’s love of the people, his benevolence. Ascending still higher, there is Zhongshan Fu, who neither swallowed the soft nor spat out the hard—that is, neither oppressed the weak nor yielded to the strong—and Yi Yin, who, knowing first, enlightened those who came to know later, and, awakening first, awakened those who came to awaken later. These were assistants to true kings and outstanding men of the Three Dynasties. How could one fail to aspire to emulate their lofty conduct?
The Book of Odes says: “Virtue is light as a feather; Zhongshan Fu lifts it.” The Book of Documents says: “Yi Yin himself and Tang both possessed a single virtue.” Virtue, then, was the foundation of these two ministers’ meritorious achievements. Its extension led to the campaign against Xia to rescue the people and to assisting Tang in becoming king over all under Heaven. Its extension also led to protecting the king’s person, serving as a model for the many lords, and promulgating clear commands throughout the four quarters. All these were applications of virtue, and the talents of an assistant to a true king cannot …

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
外矣故嘗爲之說曰王道之所以爲純者
才德出於一也伯道之所以爲雜者才德
出於二也晰王伯之幾庶可以定尚論之
學矣管見如斯不識執事以爲然否
第四問
馬化龍
同考試官教諭雷批深得闢邪崇正之意
考試官學正何批議論持正足挽近習
考試官教諭殳批意正而氣昌
===
道之不明也異端亂之也夫異端何足以
亂吾道我以其正彼以其邪若方員之異
狀也鸞梟之異音也凡有耳目者可得辨
之彼安足爲吾道病然道有時而不明焉
則異端之似吾道者亂之也夫天下物理
唯似足以亂眞彼一異端也其說乃與諸
異端者流不類而與吾道類非深於道者
孰能察之然以彼似此猶二之也又其甚
焉陰用異端之實文以儒者之言自儒者
punctuated:
外矣。故嘗爲之說曰：「王道之所以爲純者，才德出於一也；伯道之所以爲雜者，才德出於二也。」晰王伯之幾，庶可以定尚論之學矣。管見如斯，不識執事以爲然否？

第四問
馬化龍
同考試官教諭雷批：深得闢邪崇正之意。
考試官學正何批：議論持正，足挽近習。
考試官教諭殳批：意正而氣昌。

道之不明也，異端亂之也。夫異端何足以亂吾道？我以其正，彼以其邪，若方員之異狀也，鸞梟之異音也。凡有耳目者，可得辨之，彼安足爲吾道病？然道有時而不明焉，則異端之似吾道者亂之也。夫天下物理，唯似足以亂眞。彼一異端也，其說乃與諸異端者流不類，而與吾道類，非深於道者孰能察之？然以彼似此，猶二之也。又其甚焉，陰用異端之實，文以儒者之言，自儒者
translation_en:
…cannot fall outside it. Thus I once offered this explanation: “The way of the true king is pure because ability and virtue issue from a single source; the way of the hegemon is mixed because ability and virtue issue from two separate sources.” By discerning the subtle distinction between kingship and hegemony, one may perhaps establish a sound basis for the study of the ancients. Such is my limited view; I do not know whether you, sir, consider it correct.

Fourth Policy Question
Ma Hualong
Associate Examiner Lei, School Instructor, comments: “This thoroughly grasps the intent of rejecting heterodoxy and honoring orthodoxy.”
Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: “The argument upholds what is right and can counter prevailing tendencies.”
Examiner Shu, School Instructor, comments: “The intent is correct and the writing’s vital force abundant.”

When the Way is not clear, it is because heterodox teachings confuse it. Yet how could heterodox teachings suffice to confuse our Way? Ours is correct, theirs deviant: they differ as square and round differ in shape, or as the luan phoenix and the owl differ in voice. Anyone with eyes and ears can distinguish them. How, then, could they afflict our Way? Yet there are times when the Way is not clear; this happens because heterodox teachings that resemble our Way confuse it. In the nature of things under Heaven, only resemblance can confound the genuine. A teaching may be heterodox, yet its doctrines resemble our Way rather than those of the various heterodox schools. Who but someone deeply versed in the Way could detect this? Nevertheless, to say that the one resembles the other still treats them as two distinct things. There is something still worse: secretly employing the substance of heterodox teachings, embellishing it with the language of Confucian scholars, and from Confucian scholars themselves…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之口而談異端之宗㫖曰聖人之道本如
是也此則取蜾蠃而螟蛉之化而一矣學
聖人者方苦于從入之難而忽得其超詣
自便之說莫不翕然從之曰吾聖人之道
固在是也其究將化天下之爲儒者盡爲
異端擧衣冠而左衽之矣此其爲害又豈
若似之者猶有迹之可尋哉儒者苟有衞
道之心又烏容置之而不辨也夫道原于
天地具于人心本之爲五常之性發爲四
===
端之情麗爲五品之倫著爲飲食衣服宫
室器械之宜達爲禮樂刑政之具此人之
道也萬物雖與人雜然並生不得而有者
也人既具此數者必于其中各盡其所當
然之理然後無媿於爲人故學也者所以
學盡此人道也而不可以易言也由灑掃
應對而達之于精義致用由視聽言動食
息之節而達之人倫日用酬酢之間由格
致誠正而擴之於齊治均平之效由幼學
punctuated:
之口而談異端之宗㫖，曰：「聖人之道本如是也。」此則取蜾蠃而螟蛉之，化而一矣。學聖人者方苦于從入之難，而忽得其超詣自便之說，莫不翕然從之，曰：「吾聖人之道固在是也。」其究將化天下之爲儒者盡爲異端，擧衣冠而左衽之矣。此其爲害，又豈若似之者猶有迹之可尋哉？儒者苟有衞道之心，又烏容置之而不辨也？

夫道原于天地，具于人心，本之爲五常之性，發爲四端之情，麗爲五品之倫，著爲飲食衣服宫室器械之宜，達爲禮樂刑政之具。此人之道也，萬物雖與人雜然並生，不得而有者也。人既具此數者，必于其中各盡其所當然之理，然後無媿於爲人。故學也者，所以學盡此人道也，而不可以易言也。由灑掃應對而達之于精義致用，由視聽言動食息之節而達之人倫日用酬酢之間，由格致誠正而擴之於齊治均平之效，由幼學
translation_en:
…from the mouths of Confucians themselves come pronouncements of heterodox tenets, declaring: “The Way of the sages has always been thus.” This is to take the wasp and turn it into a caterpillar [?], transforming the two into one. Those studying the sages are struggling to find an entry into their teaching when they suddenly encounter these doctrines promising lofty attainment at their own convenience. Without exception, they eagerly follow them, saying: “The Way of our sages assuredly lies here.” In the end, this will transform all the Confucians in the world into followers of heterodoxy, turning the entire community of cap-and-gown wearers into people who fasten their robes on the left, in the manner of barbarians. How could the harm this causes be compared with that of teachings which merely resemble our Way and still leave traces by which they can be detected? If Confucians have any desire to defend the Way, how can they let this pass without distinguishing right from wrong?

The Way originates in Heaven and Earth and is fully present in the human heart. At its root, it constitutes the nature endowed with the five constant virtues; when expressed, it becomes the feelings of the four beginnings of virtue. It is embodied in the five human relationships, manifested in the proper provision of food and drink, clothing, dwellings, and implements, and extended into the institutions of rites, music, punishments, and government. This is the human Way: although the myriad other beings live intermingled with humankind, they cannot possess it. Since human beings are endowed with these things, they must fully realize the principles of what is right in each of them; only then can they be free of shame at being human. Learning, therefore, means learning to fulfill this human Way, and it cannot be spoken of lightly. From sprinkling and sweeping, responding and replying, one advances to refining one’s understanding of principles and putting them into practice; from regulating seeing, hearing, speech, action, eating, and resting, one extends this into human relationships and everyday dealings; from investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the heart, one broadens it into the accomplishments of ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing equity and peace to the world; from learning in childhood…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
志道以要之于終身之履歷蓋天賦人之
理本自完備人之爲學必如是而後可以
踐形故儒者之道人道之當然也聖賢之
所以爲教帝王之所以爲治非二物也昔
周之衰聖王不作孔子懼道之隱也爲之
刪詩書定禮樂贊周易脩春秋與弟子相
與講明以詔後世比七十子喪而大義遂
乖矣至孟子時去孔子僅百有餘歲而百
家之說競鳴于世是故荒唐譎詭則有若
===
莊周列禦寇名實開塞則有若申不害商
鞅孫武吳起則以其術交鬭天下之兵蘇
秦張儀則以其辯離合七國之勢以至鄒
衍之談裨海公孫龍之析堅白與夫宋鈃
尹文田駢慎到惠施之流紛紛然各徇其
偏見而自爲一方道術之爲天下裂也甚
矣孟子以孔子之道自任是宜于諸說者
拔根塞竇摧陷而廓清之爲急今觀七篇
之中略不經見其汲汲觝排而不置者則
punctuated: 志道，以要之于終身之履歷。蓋天賦人之理，本自完備；人之爲學，必如是而後可以踐形。故儒者之道，人道之當然也。聖賢之所以爲教，帝王之所以爲治，非二物也。昔周之衰，聖王不作，孔子懼道之隱也，爲之刪《詩》《書》，定禮樂，贊《周易》，脩《春秋》，與弟子相與講明，以詔後世。比七十子喪，而大義遂乖矣。至孟子時，去孔子僅百有餘歲，而百家之說競鳴于世。是故荒唐譎詭，則有若莊周、列禦寇；名實開塞，則有若申不害、商鞅；孫武、吳起，則以其術交鬭天下之兵；蘇秦、張儀，則以其辯離合七國之勢。以至鄒衍之談裨海，公孫龍之析堅白，與夫宋鈃、尹文、田駢、慎到、惠施之流，紛紛然各徇其偏見，而自爲一方，道術之爲天下裂也甚矣！孟子以孔子之道自任，是宜于諸說者，拔根塞竇，摧陷而廓清之爲急。今觀七篇之中，略不經見；其汲汲觝排而不置者，則
translation_en:
…setting one’s resolve upon the Way, and carrying this through the course of one’s entire life. The principles Heaven endows in human beings are inherently complete. Only by learning in this manner can people fulfill what their human form entails. Thus the Way of the Confucians is what the human way properly requires. The means by which sages and worthies teach and those by which emperors and kings govern are not two different things.

Formerly, when the Zhou declined and no sage king arose, Confucius feared that the Way would become obscured. He therefore edited the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents, established rites and music, elucidated the Changes of Zhou, and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals. Together with his disciples, he discussed and clarified these teachings to instruct later generations. By the time the seventy disciples had died, however, their great meaning had become distorted. In the time of Mengzi, scarcely more than a hundred years after Confucius, the teachings of the hundred schools competed for a hearing throughout the world.

Thus, for extravagant and fantastical ideas there were such men as Zhuang Zhou and Lie Yukou; for names and realities, and the opening and blocking of avenues of action, there were such men as Shen Buhai and Shang Yang. Sun Wu and Wu Qi used their techniques to set the armies of the world fighting one another; Su Qin and Zhang Yi used their eloquence to divide and unite the powers of the Seven States. Then there were Zou Yan’s discussions of the subsidiary seas, Gongsun Long’s analysis of hardness and whiteness, and the likes of Song Xing, Yin Wen, Tian Pian, Shen Dao, and Hui Shi. In a tumult, each pursued his own partial view and established a separate school. How grievously the arts of the Way had been fragmented throughout the world!

Mengzi took responsibility for upholding the Way of Confucius. It would therefore seem that his urgent task should have been to uproot these various doctrines, stop up their openings, demolish their strongholds, and sweep them away. Yet when we examine his seven books, scarcely any mention of them appears. Those whom he urgently and unceasingly opposed were…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
楊朱墨翟而已夫楊氏爲我近義墨子兼
愛近仁孟子固以仁義爲訓者乃斥二子
爲無父無君至擬於禽獸有說也夫人道
之有仁義猶天道之有陰陽廢一不可者
也二子各執其一則爲我者推其自私之
極必且敢于陷天下之至不義兼愛者推
其無辨之極必且歸于天下之至不仁使
不辭而闢之人將曰是固爲仁義者乃其
紾繆若此將不病吾之所謂仁義而疑之
===
哉故孟子之攻楊墨以其異端而似吾道
恐其亂眞也莊列之徒固不足深辨爾矣
由孟子而後能尊信孔子之道者莫若董
仲舒勸武帝罷黜百家表章六經漢之儒
者宜審於道術矣乃班固叙藝文以儒與
名法等家通爲九流者蓋世主徒有崇儒
之名而未敦敎化之本雖當世所稱大儒
亦多專門守章句鮮覩道眞又何疑于區
區文墨之士哉由董子而後能尊信孔子
punctuated:
楊朱、墨翟而已。夫楊氏爲我近義，墨子兼愛近仁。孟子固以仁義爲訓者，乃斥二子爲無父無君，至擬於禽獸，有說也。夫人道之有仁義，猶天道之有陰陽，廢一不可者也。二子各執其一，則爲我者推其自私之極，必且敢于陷天下之至不義；兼愛者推其無辨之極，必且歸于天下之至不仁。使不辭而闢之，人將曰：「是固爲仁義者，乃其紾繆若此。」將不病吾之所謂仁義而疑之哉？故孟子之攻楊墨，以其異端而似吾道，恐其亂眞也。莊列之徒，固不足深辨爾矣。
由孟子而後，能尊信孔子之道者，莫若董仲舒。勸武帝罷黜百家，表章六經，漢之儒者宜審於道術矣。乃班固叙藝文，以儒與名法等家通爲九流者，蓋世主徒有崇儒之名，而未敦敎化之本。雖當世所稱大儒，亦多專門守章句，鮮覩道眞，又何疑于區區文墨之士哉？由董子而後，能尊信孔子
translation_en:
…were only Yang Zhu and Mo Di. Yang’s doctrine of acting for oneself approaches righteousness, while Master Mo’s universal love approaches benevolence. Mencius certainly taught benevolence and righteousness; yet he denounced these two masters as acknowledging neither father nor ruler, even comparing them to beasts. There is a reason for this. Benevolence and righteousness in the human Way are like yin and yang in the Way of Heaven: neither can be dispensed with. Each of these two masters held exclusively to one. Thus, those who act for themselves, pushing selfishness to its extreme, will inevitably dare to plunge into the utmost unrighteousness in the world; those who practice universal love, pushing their lack of distinctions to its extreme, will inevitably arrive at the utmost inhumanity in the world. Had Mencius not refuted them in words, people would have said, “These are certainly practitioners of benevolence and righteousness, yet their distortions are such as this.” Would they not then have found fault with, and doubted, what we call benevolence and righteousness? Mencius therefore attacked Yang and Mo because their heterodox teachings resembled our Way, and he feared that they would confound the true with the false. Followers of Zhuangzi and Liezi, by contrast, scarcely warranted thorough refutation.
After Mencius, no one surpassed Dong Zhongshu in revering and trusting the Way of Confucius. He urged Emperor Wu to dismiss the Hundred Schools and give prominence to the Six Classics. The Confucian scholars of the Han should therefore have clearly understood the Way and its teachings. Yet Ban Gu, in his bibliographical account, grouped the Confucians together with the School of Names, the Legalists, and other schools as the Nine Currents. This was presumably because rulers had merely the reputation of honoring Confucian learning, without strengthening the foundations of moral instruction. Even those acclaimed in their day as great Confucian scholars mostly confined themselves to particular scholarly traditions and adhered to textual divisions and explanations; few perceived the truth of the Way. Why, then, should we be surprised at mere men of letters? After Master Dong, the one who could revere and trust Confucius…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之道者莫若韓愈于時佛老之敎布濩中
國自天子達于庶人鮮不震動崇奉愈乃
昌言排之瀕死不懾且自任與孟子闢楊
墨同功夫孟子之闢楊墨嚴矣愈之書往
往以孔墨竝稱其傳王承福復稱其道似
楊朱是尚未明孟子深拒之意矧當其時
緇黃之徒第以禍福報應恐脅流俗愈之
所以闢之亦徒以是故耳不足多也迨至
大宋濂洛關閩諸儒出始有以發揮人道
之大經闡明聖賢之本旨辨學者用工之
先後以著入道之次第蓋自孟子之後道
之湮廢千有餘年而復明可謂盛矣然當
其時蔥嶺餘敎幻發禪宗而吾黨之士譎
誕好奇者初攘莊列之緒餘繼倣儒道之
形象為之累架中間微辭隱義有近於六
經之旨矣故程子曰古釋氏只是崇設像
敎其害至小今日之風便先言性命先驅
耳智者才愈高明則陷溺愈深朱子曰釋
punctuated:
之道者，莫若韓愈。于時佛老之敎布濩中國，自天子達于庶人，鮮不震動崇奉。愈乃昌言排之，瀕死不懾，且自任與孟子闢楊墨同功。夫孟子之闢楊墨嚴矣，愈之書往往以孔墨竝稱，其傳王承福，復稱其道似楊朱，是尚未明孟子深拒之意，矧當其時緇黃之徒第以禍福報應恐脅流俗，愈之所以闢之亦徒以是故耳，不足多也。
迨至大宋，濂洛關閩諸儒出，始有以發揮人道之大經，闡明聖賢之本旨，辨學者用工之先後，以著入道之次第。蓋自孟子之後，道之湮廢千有餘年而復明，可謂盛矣。然當其時，蔥嶺餘敎幻發禪宗，而吾黨之士譎誕好奇者，初攘莊列之緒餘，繼倣儒道之形象，為之累架，中間微辭隱義，有近於六經之旨矣。故程子曰：「古釋氏只是崇設像敎，其害至小。今日之風，便先言性命，先驅耳。智者才愈高明，則陷溺愈深。」朱子曰：「釋
translation_en:
…the Way, none equaled Han Yu. At that time, the teachings of Buddhism and Laozi had spread throughout China. From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, scarcely anyone failed to be awed by them and to revere them. Han Yu openly denounced them; even when near death, he remained undaunted. He further claimed for himself an achievement equal to Mengzi’s refutation of Yang Zhu and Mo Di. Yet Mengzi had been uncompromising in rejecting Yang and Mo, whereas Han Yu’s writings often mentioned Kongzi and Mo Di together. In his biography of Wang Chengfu, he even said that Wang’s way resembled that of Yang Zhu. Thus he had not yet understood Mengzi’s reasons for rejecting them so firmly. Moreover, the black-robed Buddhist monks and yellow-robed Daoists of his day merely intimidated ordinary people with threats of calamity and promises of blessings through karmic recompense. Han Yu likewise rejected them merely on these grounds. This does not merit much praise.
Only when the scholars of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min emerged under the great Song dynasty were the cardinal principles of the human Way brought fully to light, the fundamental intentions of the sages and worthies elucidated, and the proper order of scholarly effort distinguished, thereby making clear the stages of entering the Way. After Mengzi, the Way had been obscured and neglected for more than a thousand years before becoming clear again. This may indeed be called a flourishing age. Yet at that time the lingering teaching from the Congling mountains conjured up the Chan school. Those among our own scholars who were deceitful, extravagant, and fond of novelty first appropriated the remnants of Zhuangzi and Liezi, then imitated the outward forms of the Confucian Way, building up a framework for it. Among its subtle expressions and hidden meanings were some that approached the purport of the Six Classics. Thus Master Cheng said: “The Buddhists of antiquity merely exalted and established teachings centered on images; the harm they caused was very slight. The fashion today is immediately to speak of human nature and Heaven’s mandate, taking the lead [?]. The more brilliant the abilities of intelligent people, the more deeply they become ensnared.” Master Zhu said: “The Buddhist…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
氏之書極有高妙處句句與自家不同吾
儒多有折而入之當時若王介甫之學張
無垢之學庸解呂氏之大學解大段以佛
義文儒道駸駸然布彗孛而翳日月引支
孽而亂宗系矣夫釋者之言近吾道固足
病矣然人知其爲釋氏之言也則有識者
尤得而決擇也今也以談道之儒折聖賢
之言而所述者皆翻達磨慧可之窠臼改
大能宗杲之面目使后生晚進汩沒其中
===
終身不知人之所以爲道儒之所以爲學
者則其害豈在洪水猛獸下哉故程朱二
子不專攻二氏而必先極力辨明乎此者
以其流患之若是甚也嗚呼數子者之繆
得程朱之說闢之亦旣有瘳矣今世之士
莫不誦法孔孟析義程朱使皆明于人道
之當然而從事于儒者之學豈非儒敎世
風之一大幸惜也程朱不作而世儒之高
邁不羈厭聖學之嚴密而憚于始終條理
punctuated: 氏之書極有高妙處，句句與自家不同，吾儒多有折而入之。」當時若王介甫之學、張無垢之學庸解、呂氏之大學解，大段以佛義文儒道，駸駸然布彗孛而翳日月，引支孽而亂宗系矣。夫釋者之言近吾道，固足病矣；然人知其爲釋氏之言也，則有識者尤得而決擇也。今也，以談道之儒折聖賢之言，而所述者皆翻達磨慧可之窠臼，改大能宗杲之面目，使后生晚進汩沒其中，終身不知人之所以爲道、儒之所以爲學者，則其害豈在洪水猛獸下哉？故程朱二子不專攻二氏，而必先極力辨明乎此者，以其流患之若是甚也。嗚呼！數子者之繆，得程朱之說闢之，亦旣有瘳矣。今世之士莫不誦法孔孟，析義程朱，使皆明于人道之當然而從事于儒者之學，豈非儒敎世風之一大幸？惜也，程朱不作，而世儒之高邁不羈、厭聖學之嚴密而憚于始終條理
translation_en:
…“Buddhist writings contain passages of extraordinary subtlety, yet every sentence differs from our own teachings. Many of our Confucian scholars have nevertheless bent their own teachings to accommodate them.” At that time, such works as the teachings of Wang Jiefu, Zhang Wugou’s Explanation of the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean [?], and Master Lü’s Explanation of the Great Learning extensively used Buddhist ideas to embellish the Confucian Way. Increasingly, they spread comets across the heavens to obscure the sun and moon, and introduced collateral and illegitimate branches to confound the line of descent. That Buddhist statements resemble our Way is certainly cause for concern. Yet when people recognize them as Buddhist statements, those with discernment can still distinguish and choose between them. Now, however, men who discourse on the Way as Confucians distort the words of the sages and worthies, while everything they expound merely reworks the old patterns of Damo and Huike and gives a new appearance to Daneng [?] and Zonggao. They cause younger students and later followers to become submerged in these teachings, remaining ignorant throughout their lives of what constitutes the human Way and what constitutes Confucian learning. Can the harm they cause be any less than that of floods and savage beasts? Thus the two masters Cheng and Zhu did not devote themselves solely to attacking Buddhism and Daoism, but first made every effort to clarify these distinctions, because the resulting harm was so grave.

Alas! The errors of those thinkers had already been substantially remedied through the refutations supplied by Cheng and Zhu. Scholars today all recite and take as their models Confucius and Mencius, and analyze principles through Cheng and Zhu. If all were to understand what is proper to the human Way and devote themselves to Confucian learning, would this not be a great blessing for Confucian teaching and the moral climate of the age? Regrettably, Cheng and Zhu no longer arise among us, while those present-day Confucians who are lofty and unrestrained, who dislike the rigor of the sages’ learning and shrink from the orderly progression from beginning to end…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之難者乃不勝一切自便之私拾楊簡陸
九淵之賸餘而宗祖于張呂作弄精神驅
駕氣勢借先儒之文字傳黠僧之衣鉢將
鼓一世而悉異教之從未能下學也而徑
求上達世豈有今日適越而昔至者哉未
能循迹也而自謂安心世豈有外肆跳踉
而中致肅者哉詖淫邪遁靡所底止使後
學之士猖狂恣肆而不肯便辟近裏從事
于切巳之實學其究足以壞人心蠹國政
===
西晉玄虛之效往事可明鑒矣有世道之
責者誠不可不深辨而力挽之也挽之何
如亦曰明人道之本原陳聖學之次第以
先于自治而巳
第五問
王憲
考試官學正何批深識裕民足國之計子其
有適用之學者錄之
考試官教諭艾批經濟之略籌畫允當
punctuated:
之難者，乃不勝一切自便之私，拾楊簡陸九淵之賸餘，而宗祖于張呂，作弄精神，驅駕氣勢，借先儒之文字，傳黠僧之衣鉢，將鼓一世而悉異教之從。未能下學也，而徑求上達，世豈有今日適越而昔至者哉？未能循迹也，而自謂安心，世豈有外肆跳踉而中致肅者哉？詖淫邪遁，靡所底止，使後學之士猖狂恣肆，而不肯便辟近裏，從事于切巳之實學，其究足以壞人心，蠹國政。西晉玄虛之效，往事可明鑒矣。有世道之責者，誠不可不深辨而力挽之也。挽之何如？亦曰明人道之本原，陳聖學之次第，以先于自治而巳。
第五問
王憲
考試官學正何批：「深識裕民足國之計，子其有適用之學者，錄之。」
考試官教諭艾批：「經濟之略，籌畫允當。」
translation_en:
…the difficulty, instead succumb to every selfish desire for their own convenience. They pick up the remnants of Yang Jian’s and Lu Jiuyuan’s teachings and take Zhang and Lü as their patriarchs, manipulating the spirit and marshaling forceful displays. Borrowing the writings of earlier Confucians, they transmit the robe and bowl of crafty Buddhist monks, seeking to stir up an entire age into following heterodox teachings. Before they can learn the things below, they seek directly to attain understanding of the things above. Can anyone in this world set out for Yue today and have arrived yesterday? Before they can follow the proper traces, they claim to have set their minds at peace. Can anyone give free rein to leaping and capering outwardly while attaining reverence within? Their biased, extravagant, perverse, and evasive words know no bounds. They lead later students into wild abandon and unrestrained conduct, unwilling to turn inward [?] and engage in substantive learning that bears directly upon themselves. Ultimately, this is enough to corrupt people’s hearts and undermine the government. The consequences of the Western Jin’s devotion to abstruse emptiness offer a clear warning from the past. Those responsible for the moral order of the age must indeed distinguish these matters thoroughly and strive to reverse this trend. How should they reverse it? Simply by clarifying the fundamental source of the human Way and setting forth the successive stages of sagely learning, beginning with putting themselves in order.
Fifth Question
Wang Xian
Examiner He, School Director, comments: “You understand deeply the means of enriching the people and ensuring the state’s sufficiency. You surely possess learning suited to practical application. Accept this essay.”
Examiner Ai, Instructor, comments: “The strategies for ordering the realm and assisting its people are soundly and appropriately planned.”

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
天下有自然之利也貴乎有以導而布之
是故上焉國用之足者足以比也下焉民
用之裕者裕以此也乃上下兼利之道誠
盛世之首務而臣工之所當亟亟焉以究心
者也故欲足國而不求諸自然之利則爲
權謀爲術數國用必不可得而足矣欲裕
民而不求諸自然之利則爲私恩爲小惠
民用必不可得而裕矣惟以利之自然者
導而布之則國不期足而自足蘇子所謂
===
萬世之計者是也民不期裕而自裕孔子
所謂不費之惠者是也則利豈
國家之諱言哉此大學生財之大道所以爲
治平天下之要也執事策士終篇而以水
田詢及蓋欲爲斯民稽厚生之本而爲
國家立裕用之原甚盛心也愚也敢不悉心
以對且水田之說何所昉乎井田之遺也
井田莫備於周而非始于周也虞書曰予
決九川距四海濬畎澮距川是也亦非始
punctuated:
天下有自然之利也，貴乎有以導而布之。是故上焉國用之足者，足以比也；下焉民用之裕者，裕以此也。乃上下兼利之道，誠盛世之首務，而臣工之所當亟亟焉以究心者也。故欲足國而不求諸自然之利，則爲權謀，爲術數，國用必不可得而足矣；欲裕民而不求諸自然之利，則爲私恩，爲小惠，民用必不可得而裕矣。惟以利之自然者導而布之，則國不期足而自足，蘇子所謂萬世之計者是也；民不期裕而自裕，孔子所謂不費之惠者是也。則利豈國家之諱言哉？此《大學》生財之大道，所以爲治平天下之要也。
執事策士終篇，而以水田詢及，蓋欲爲斯民稽厚生之本，而爲國家立裕用之原，甚盛心也。愚也敢不悉心以對？且水田之說何所昉乎？井田之遺也。井田莫備於周，而非始于周也。《虞書》曰：「予決九川距四海，濬畎澮距川。」是也。亦非始
translation_en:
There are benefits naturally available in the world; what matters is finding ways to channel and distribute them. Thus, above, the state’s expenditures are adequately supplied through these [?]; below, the people’s needs are amply supplied through them. This way of benefiting both those above and those below is indeed the foremost task of a flourishing age, and something to which officials ought urgently to devote their minds. If one wishes to provide sufficiently for the state without seeking these natural benefits, one resorts to expedients and calculations, and the state’s needs can never be adequately supplied. If one wishes to enrich the people without seeking these natural benefits, one resorts to personal favors and petty kindnesses, and the people’s needs can never be amply supplied. Only by channeling and distributing the benefits naturally available will the state attain sufficiency of itself, without deliberately seeking it: this is what Master Su called “a plan for ten thousand generations.” The people, too, will attain abundance of themselves, without deliberately seeking it: this is what Confucius called “beneficence without expense.” Why, then, should benefit be something the state avoids mentioning? This is the great way of producing wealth described in the Great Learning, and the reason it is essential to bringing order and peace to all under Heaven.
At the end of your policy questions for the candidates, you, honored examiners, inquire about irrigated fields. Surely you wish to investigate the foundations of a prosperous livelihood for these people and establish a source of ample resources for the state. This is a most admirable intention. Ignorant though I am, how could I dare not devote my whole mind to replying? Where, then, did the practice of irrigated fields originate? It is a legacy of the well-field system. That system reached its fullest development under the Zhou, but it did not begin under the Zhou. The Book of Yu says: “I opened channels for the nine rivers to reach the four seas, and deepened the field channels and drains to reach the rivers.” This is evidence of it. Nor did it begin …

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
於虞也通典曰黃帝時八家爲井井開四
道而分八宅鑿井於中是也蓋井田之說
其來遠矣至周而其法始詳有遂人十夫
爲溝百夫爲洫千夫爲澮萬夫爲川之制
焉有稻人以潴畜水以防止水以溝蕩水
以遂均水以列舍水以澮寫水之制焉又
有匠人氏辨其深廣之度通其蓄洩之宜
焉法至善矣當其時三年耕餘一年之食
九年耕餘三年之食以三十年之通制國
===
用民安物阜公私充足太和在成周宇宙
間矣自阡陌旣開而井田之法廢經界不
正而溝洫之制湮識治體者往往慨古法
之善而無可復之期此執事所以深致意
于水田之利非謂其得古之遺意乎黃帝
之敎曰有石城十仞湯池百步帶甲百萬
而無粟弗能守也鼂錯之說曰珠玉黃金
饑不可食寒不可衣然而衆貴之者以上
用之故也粟米布帛生於地長於時聚於
punctuated:
於虞也。《通典》曰：「黃帝時，八家爲井，井開四道而分八宅，鑿井於中。」是也。蓋井田之說，其來遠矣。至周而其法始詳，有遂人十夫爲溝、百夫爲洫、千夫爲澮、萬夫爲川之制焉；有稻人以潴畜水、以防止水、以溝蕩水、以遂均水、以列舍水、以澮寫水之制焉；又有匠人氏辨其深廣之度，通其蓄洩之宜焉。法至善矣。當其時，三年耕，餘一年之食；九年耕，餘三年之食。以三十年之通制國用，民安物阜，公私充足，太和在成周宇宙間矣。
自阡陌旣開而井田之法廢，經界不正而溝洫之制湮。識治體者，往往慨古法之善而無可復之期。此執事所以深致意于水田之利，非謂其得古之遺意乎？黃帝之敎曰：「有石城十仞，湯池百步，帶甲百萬，而無粟，弗能守也。」鼂錯之說曰：「珠玉黃金，饑不可食，寒不可衣。然而衆貴之者，以上用之故也。粟米布帛，生於地，長於時，聚於
translation_en:
…in the time of Yu either. The Comprehensive Institutions (Tongdian) states: “In the time of the Yellow Emperor, eight households constituted a well-field unit. Four roads were opened through it, dividing it into eight homesteads, with a well dug in the center.” This is the evidence. The well-field system thus has a very ancient origin. Only under the Zhou did its regulations become detailed. The Director of Rural Affairs administered a system in which ten cultivators’ holdings shared a ditch, one hundred a larger channel, one thousand a main drainage channel, and ten thousand a river channel. The Rice-field Officer administered a system that stored water in reservoirs, checked it with embankments, conducted it through ditches, distributed it evenly through small channels, released it through rows of channels, and drained it through main channels. The master craftsmen further determined the proper depths and widths and ensured suitable arrangements for retaining and discharging water. These regulations were excellent indeed. In those days, three years of cultivation yielded a surplus sufficient for one year’s food; nine years yielded a surplus sufficient for three years’ food. State expenditure was regulated on the basis of an overall reckoning of thirty years. The people lived securely, goods were abundant, and public and private stores were ample. Supreme harmony prevailed throughout the realm of the flourishing Zhou.
Once the paths dividing privately held fields were opened, the well-field system was abandoned; as field boundaries ceased to be properly ordered, the system of ditches and channels fell into oblivion. Those who understand the essentials of government often lament that, excellent as the ancient institutions were, there is no prospect of restoring them. Is this not why you, honored examiners, give such earnest attention to the benefits of irrigated fields—because you consider them to preserve something of the ancient intent? The Yellow Emperor’s teaching says: “Even with stone walls ten ren high, a moat of boiling water one hundred paces wide, and a million armored soldiers, without grain one cannot hold out.” Chao Cuo’s argument says: “Pearls, jade, and gold cannot be eaten when one is hungry or worn when one is cold. Yet the multitude prizes them because those above make use of them. Grain and cloth are produced from the earth, grow with the seasons, and are accumulated through…”

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
力非可一日成也一日弗得則饑寒至是
故明君貴五穀而賤金玉由是觀之農非
國之本而地非財之源乎民生國計之攸
關可槩見矣我
國家定鼎燕京百官六軍羣工吏胥所食米
粟歲計何啻億萬皆漕運于東南給焉非
以有水田之饒乎夫農之致力於田也水
陸□不相遠而其收穫也則或相十倍焉
以陸田懸命于天而水田取必于人其利
===
害大相逕庭者東南之饒于財賦有以也
邇來東南民力漸以困竭輓運削弱司農
告匱乏三歲之計有識者無隱憂邪夫天
下之勢譬之一家也有富民焉而城居負
郭之田無可資惟取足以別業焉其無遠
圖可知矣東南偏處一隅
國家之別業也河南諸省附近郊圻
國家之負郭也以東南一隅而獨當
國家之全給無恠乎力之竭而用不裕也諸
punctuated:
力，非可一日成也。一日弗得，則饑寒至。是故明君貴五穀而賤金玉。由是觀之，農非國之本，而地非財之源乎？民生國計之攸關，可槩見矣。
我國家定鼎燕京，百官六軍、羣工吏胥所食米粟，歲計何啻億萬，皆漕運于東南給焉，非以有水田之饒乎？夫農之致力於田也，水陸□不相遠，而其收穫也，則或相十倍焉。以陸田懸命于天，而水田取必于人，其利害大相逕庭者，東南之饒于財賦有以也。
邇來東南民力漸以困竭，輓運削弱，司農告匱，乏三歲之計，有識者無隱憂邪？夫天下之勢，譬之一家也。有富民焉，而城居負郭之田無可資，惟取足以別業焉，其無遠圖可知矣。東南偏處一隅，國家之別業也；河南諸省附近郊圻，國家之負郭也。以東南一隅而獨當國家之全給，無恠乎力之竭而用不裕也。諸
translation_en:
…labor; they cannot be produced in a single day. Yet if one goes without them for a single day, hunger and cold arrive. Thus an enlightened ruler values the five grains and holds gold and jade cheap. Viewed in this light, is agriculture not the foundation of the state, and land the source of wealth? Their importance to the people’s livelihood and the state’s finances is readily apparent.
Our dynasty established its capital at Yanjing. The rice and grain consumed by the officials, the six armies, the various artisans, and the clerks and runners amount annually to hundreds of millions and more. All are supplied by grain transport from the southeast. Is this not because of its abundant irrigated fields? The labor farmers devote to irrigated and dry fields does not differ greatly [?], yet their yields may differ tenfold. Dry fields depend on Heaven for their survival, whereas irrigated fields offer assured results through human effort. Their advantages and disadvantages differ so greatly: there is good reason why the southeast is rich in fiscal resources.
Recently, the resources of the people in the southeast have gradually become exhausted, grain transport has weakened, and the fiscal authorities report depleted reserves, with insufficient provision for three years. Can discerning men be free of private anxiety? The circumstances of the realm may be compared to those of a household. Suppose a wealthy man lives in a city but has no fields outside its walls on which he can draw, relying entirely on a separate estate to meet his needs. His lack of foresight is plain. The southeast, situated in a remote corner, is the state’s separate estate; Henan and the other provinces near the capital region are its fields outside the city walls. If the southeastern corner alone must bear the entire burden of supplying the state, it is no wonder that its resources are exhausted and its supplies inadequate. As for the various…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
省姑無論已河南民生耳目所觀擊者殆
可痛也高阜之地間種菽麥而鞠爲榛莽
者彌望也潢汙沮洳則視爲無用而輕棄
之一遇旱澇則束手無策甘流邪僻以苟
旦夕之生而已夫地之爲道高下相因皆
以資生萬物養育萬民本無分於南北東
西矧南方山坡峻薄較之北方土厚水深
平原接壤尤爲不同且三代井田之制皆
始于此豈南可以爲水田而北獨不可爲
===
邪惟民有遺力斯地有遺利而民之所以
有遺力者特在上之人鼓舞勸相之無術
耳仰稽前代興水利於兩河之内者豈鮮
其人哉魏西門豹之爲鄴令也太史公稱
其問民疾苦鑿渠灌田而傳漢書者乃載
文起責之之言曰魏氏之行田也以百畝
鄴獨二百畝漳水在其旁豹不知用是不
知也知而不興是不仁也魏于是以起爲
鄴令遂引漳水溉鄴以富河内而民歌賢
punctuated:
省姑無論已，河南民生，耳目所觀擊者，殆可痛也。高阜之地，間種菽麥，而鞠爲榛莽者彌望也。潢汙沮洳，則視爲無用而輕棄之。一遇旱澇，則束手無策，甘流邪僻，以苟旦夕之生而已。夫地之爲道，高下相因，皆以資生萬物，養育萬民，本無分於南北東西。矧南方山坡峻薄，較之北方土厚水深、平原接壤，尤爲不同。且三代井田之制，皆始于此，豈南可以爲水田，而北獨不可爲邪？惟民有遺力，斯地有遺利，而民之所以有遺力者，特在上之人鼓舞勸相之無術耳。
仰稽前代，興水利於兩河之内者，豈鮮其人哉？魏西門豹之爲鄴令也，太史公稱其問民疾苦，鑿渠灌田。而傳漢書者，乃載文起責之之言曰：「魏氏之行田也，以百畝，鄴獨二百畝。漳水在其旁，豹不知用，是不知也；知而不興，是不仁也。」魏于是以起爲鄴令，遂引漳水溉鄴，以富河内，而民歌賢
translation_en:
…the other provinces may be left aside for now. As for the people's livelihood in Henan, what one sees and hears [?] is truly distressing. On the uplands, beans and wheat are planted here and there, but land abandoned to thickets stretches as far as the eye can see. Pools and marshy lowlands are regarded as useless and casually abandoned. Whenever drought or flooding strikes, the people are helpless, with no remedy; they resign themselves to falling into illicit ways merely to scrape through another day. By its nature, the land's high and low places complement one another: all serve to bring forth the myriad things and nourish the people, without distinction between south, north, east, and west. Moreover, the steep slopes and thin soils of the south differ markedly from the deep soils, ample waters, and continuous stretches of level plain in the north. The well-field system of the Three Dynasties also originated here. How could the south be made into irrigated fields while the north alone could not? It is because the people's labor remains unused that the land's benefits remain unrealized. And the people's labor remains unused solely because those above them lack the means to inspire, encourage, and assist them.
Looking back to earlier dynasties, were there few who developed irrigation in the regions on either side of the Yellow River? When Ximen Bao of Wei served as Magistrate of Ye, the Grand Historian says that he inquired into the people's hardships and dug channels to irrigate their fields. Yet an account transmitting the History of the Han [?] records Wen Qi's [?] criticism of him: “In Wei, land is allotted at one hundred mu, but in Ye alone it is two hundred mu. The Zhang River runs alongside it. If Bao does not know how to use it, that is ignorance; if he knows but does not undertake the work, that is inhumanity.” Wei thereupon appointed Qi Magistrate of Ye. He then diverted the Zhang River to irrigate Ye, enriching Henei, and the people sang in praise of his worthiness…

title: 隆慶四年河南鄉試錄
text:
今史氏所載雖有不同豈豹以先民未之
爲而不知其可以有爲乎抑豹開其始而
未竟起則更加疏鑿以成之乎厥後開稻
田數百頃視事七年政化大行而有天降
神明君之歌者則汲縣令崔瑗也通溝瀆
起水門歲漑田至三萬頃繼之者復脩治
陂池廣拓土田而民有召父杜母之語者
則南陽守召信臣杜詩也激用滍淯諸水
以浸原田萬餘頃分疆刻石眾庶賴之者
===
則大將軍杜預乎帥軍于倉陵立堰漑田
千餘頃歲收穀百餘萬石以充儲備兼贍
貧人者非豫州刺史夏侯楙乎之數人者
或度其高下而導引之或尋其成迹而脩
濬之咸以致富强于當時垂休聲于後世
取而法之顧不可歟元泰定間學士虞集
議用浙人之法築隄捍水漑京東瀕海之
田其法非不鑿鑿可行也竟爲浮言所阻
及至正間海運不至京師乏食宰臣思集
punctuated:
今史氏所載雖有不同，豈豹以先民未之爲而不知其可以有爲乎？抑豹開其始而未竟，起則更加疏鑿以成之乎？厥後開稻田數百頃，視事七年，政化大行，而有「天降神明君」之歌者，則汲縣令崔瑗也。通溝瀆，起水門，歲漑田至三萬頃，繼之者復脩治陂池，廣拓土田，而民有「召父杜母」之語者，則南陽守召信臣、杜詩也。激用滍淯諸水，以浸原田萬餘頃，分疆刻石，眾庶賴之者，則大將軍杜預乎？帥軍于倉陵，立堰漑田千餘頃，歲收穀百餘萬石，以充儲備，兼贍貧人者，非豫州刺史夏侯楙乎？之數人者，或度其高下而導引之，或尋其成迹而脩濬之，咸以致富强于當時，垂休聲于後世。取而法之，顧不可歟？
元泰定間，學士虞集議用浙人之法，築隄捍水，漑京東瀕海之田。其法非不鑿鑿可行也，竟爲浮言所阻。及至正間，海運不至，京師乏食，宰臣思集
translation_en:
